assessment.nobel_worthiness: Founded the law-and-finance field. It shows how legal institutions and investor protection shape financial development, ownership structure and corporate governance. It has very broad influence across finance, law and development, and a large empirical literature has grown from it.
assessment.attribution: The LLSV papers (La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer, Vishny) are the core. Shleifer, La Porta and Lopez-de-Silanes are the most consistently credited trio. Vishny is a close fourth, and the three-laureate cap forces a difficult exclusion.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from the late 1990s and has been replicated, extended and debated for about 25 years, so it is fully mature.
uncertainties: The legal-origins thesis has been challenged on causal identification and on the coding of legal rules.
Shleifer's separate contributions to behavioural finance and privatization blur the boundary of the citation.
I rely on memory of the literature and have not verified any source independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The heterogeneous-firm model of trade changed how economists understand selection, reallocation and the gains from trade. It also changed empirical work on exporters. Its influence on trade theory and on the interpretation of firm-level data is large.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution. Helpman, with Melitz and Yeaple, made the key extensions to FDI and exporting, and Helpman's earlier trade theory adds weight. Redding's contributions are mainly on quantitative and spatial extensions.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of confirmation, with widespread policy use. Krugman's 2008 prize covered related new trade theory but not firm heterogeneity.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as distinct enough from Krugman's prize.
Whether Redding or Bernard and Jensen should share credit; Bernard and Jensen are not on this ballot entry.
Some quantitative implications depend on functional-form assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Provides the workhorse methods for estimating demand and supply in differentiated-product markets, plus dynamic industry models. These methods underpin merger analysis, competition policy and a large part of applied microeconomics. The influence is deep and has had real policy impact.
assessment.attribution: BLP (Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes 1995) is the clearest common reference, and Pakes also led the dynamic-games and Ericson-Pakes work. Bresnahan, Bajari, Benkard and others made related contributions, so the group is crowded.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of continuous use and refinement, so it is very mature.
uncertainties: Attribution is spread over many contributors, and any three-name cut leaves out important people such as Bresnahan.
A methodological prize raises the question of whether the economic discovery or the technique is being rewarded.
I am a specialist in an adjacent IO area, so I should guard against overrating this field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based approach to technology and labour demand, together with the China-shock evidence on local labour markets, reshaped understanding of wage inequality, automation and the distributional costs of trade. Its policy salience is very high.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both strands. Hanson, with Autor and Dorn, anchors the trade-shock work. Katz brings the earlier skill-biased technical change literature. Dorn and Acemoglu have close links to the task work, and Acemoglu has already been honoured.
assessment.maturity: The roughly 15 years of work is solid, but the long-run effects and the persistence of the China shock are still debated.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 and 2023 prizes in technology and labour.
Whether the China-shock findings are durable and generalize beyond the US.
The credit split between task-model theory and the empirical trade-shock papers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities, Calvo pricing, the Taylor rule and the New Keynesian synthesis underpin modern monetary policy analysis and central-bank practice. The importance is very high.
assessment.attribution: The credit is spread across many people: Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Evans, Smets and Wouters, and Gertler. Any three-name selection is arbitrary to some degree, and the three chosen reflect foundational pricing and rule contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been confirmed in practice over roughly 30 years, though the 2021-23 inflation episode tested parts of it.
uncertainties: Attribution is highly diffuse and this is the biggest weakness.
The inflation episode has revived debate about the Phillips curve and the framework's adequacy.
Overlap with earlier macro prizes such as Lucas, Sargent and Sims, Kydland and Prescott, and Bernanke.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shows how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks, which provides the core theory of credit cycles. It is the central framework for financial frictions in macroeconomics and was very influential after 2008.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) is the key paper. Gertler adds the financial accelerator and later intermediary work, and Bernanke, Gertler and Gilchrist's accelerator partly overlaps with Bernanke's 2022 prize.
assessment.maturity: Nearly 30 years of use, with strong empirical and policy influence after the global financial crisis.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises.
Gertler's presence on both this entry and B040.
Whether the committee would treat Gilchrist as a necessary co-recipient.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Combines empirical sufficient-statistics methods, taxable-income elasticities and behavioural responses to taxation into a modern empirical basis for optimal tax analysis. It has clear policy relevance and large influence in public economics.
assessment.attribution: Saez is the main figure, and Slemrod represents the tax-compliance and avoidance tradition. Chetty is a leading figure, but his work on other topics (mobility, B041) dilutes this specific citation. Feldstein's foundational ETI work is not creditable, as he is deceased.
assessment.maturity: The ETI literature has matured over 25 years. The newer sufficient-statistics work is influential but younger.
uncertainties: Chetty and Saez also appear on other ballot entries, which raises questions about how the discovery is defined.
Elasticity estimates are sensitive to context and identification.
Stantcheva's contributions are comparatively recent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic panel GMM estimators are used throughout applied economics, in growth, firm and labour studies. The methods are very widely adopted and enable much empirical research.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond (1991) and Arellano and Bover and Blundell and Bond (1998) are the standard citations. Blundell has a broader record in labour and consumption, and Holtz-Eakin, Newey and Rosen and Anderson and Hsiao are antecedents.
assessment.maturity: About 30 years of use. The method is mature, and its weaknesses (instrument proliferation, weak instruments) are well understood.
uncertainties: The contribution is a methodological toolkit more than a discovery, so the committee may weigh it differently.
Known weaknesses with many instruments and persistent series.
Overlap with antecedent work and with other econometrics entries such as B021 and B030.
